title: Bobkov inequality for finite coordinates
statement: Let $I$ be a finite set and let $f:\{0,1\}^I\to\mathbb R$ take values in $[0,1]$. Under independent uniform bits, define $D_i f(x)=\bigl(f(x^{i\leftarrow0})-f(x^{i\leftarrow1})\bigr)/2$, where $x^{i\leftarrow b}$ sets coordinate $i$ to $b$. Then $\overline I(\mathbb E f)\le\mathbb E\sqrt{\overline I(f)^2+\sum_{i\in I}(D_i f)^2}$.
hypotheses_covered: A real-valued function on Boolean vectors indexed by I
replaced: Let $\Phi,\varphi$ be the standard Gaussian distribution function and density, and let $\overline I(p)=\varphi(\Phi^{-1}(p))$ for $0<p<1$, with $\overline I(p)=0$ elsewhere. Let $I$ be finite and $f:\{0,1\}^I\to[0,1]$. Under the independent uniform bit law, $\overline I(\mathbb E f)\le\mathbb E\sqrt{\overline I(f)^2+\sum_{i\in I}(D_i f)^2}$, where $D_i f(x)=(f(x^{i\leftarrow0})-f(x^{i\leftarrow1}))/2$.
